title: UN Security Council adopts Resolution 2803 endorsing Trump's Gaza plan and a stabilization force
body:
On Monday 17 November 2025, the United Nations Security Council adopted Resolution 2803 with 13 votes in favour and none against, while China and Russia abstained. The resolution endorsed the peace plan for Gaza put forward by US President Donald Trump and welcomed his Comprehensive Plan announced on 29 September 2025. UN News noted that the first phase of the 20-point plan had led to a ceasefire between Hamas and Israel days later.

The resolution welcomed the creation of a Board of Peace as a transitional administration in Gaza to coordinate reconstruction. It authorized the Board of Peace to set up a temporary International Stabilization Force, which would deploy under a unified command the Board found acceptable. Countries contributing personnel were to do so in close consultation with Egypt and Israel.

US Ambassador Mike Waltz called the resolution another significant step towards a stable Gaza and said the force would stabilize security, support Gaza's demilitarization, dismantle terrorist infrastructure, decommission weapons and protect Palestinian civilians. Algeria's ambassador Amar Bendjama credited Trump's efforts but said lasting peace was impossible without justice for the Palestinian people. Russia's ambassador Vasily Nebenzya explained his country's abstention, arguing that the Council was endorsing a US initiative based on Washington's promises and giving full control of Gaza to the Board of Peace and the stabilization force, whose details remained unknown.
